output:
I'll start by reading the docs and looking at the data layout.

I've read the rules. Next I'll write the script.

I wrote `/app/bin/tally.py` and ran it on `/app/data` to produce `/app/out/tally.json`. It matches the certified results.

- **Unit tests:** `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` ran 4 tests and all passed.
- **Certified check:** `python tools/check_tally.py` matched 7 of 7 contests and 31 of 31 rounds.

The script uses only the standard library. I wrote it from the rules in `/app/docs` rather than from what the current data contains, so it should hold up on other elections. I also wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

One choice the docs don't settle: if a candidate is missing from `lot_order`, the script treats it as coming before every listed candidate. The docs say `lot_order` lists every candidate, so this should never come up with valid input.

command_result.command: cd /app; ls -R docs tests tools bin out 2>&1 | head -50; ls data | head -30; cat docs/overview.md
cd /app/docs; cat election.md records.md counting.md output.md changelog.md

cd /app; ls data/cvr | head; ls data/cvr | wc -l; head -c 1500 data/election.json; for f in $(ls data/cvr/* | head -3); do echo == $f; head -12 $f; done; cat tests/test_tally.py | head -40; ls tests/fixtures/*/input/cvr; python3 --version
cd /app; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -20; python3 bin/tally.py data out/tally.json && python tools/check_tally.py

cd /app; echo '{"status":"success","summary":"Wrote /app/bin/tally.py following the documented rules and ran it on /app/data to produce /app/out/tally.json. The unit tests pass and check_tally.py reports 7 of 7 contests and 31 of 31 rounds matching."}' > STATUS.json; cat STATUS.json
